issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts hard or fails
issues.sym: Harsh 1-2 upshifts or hard downshifts once warm, slipping, a transmission warning, or a car that will not move.
issues.why: The 4- and 5-speed automatics in these cars wear internally with age and mileage. Owners report full failures from about 90,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have the codes read. A fluid service sometimes helps mild shift problems; slipping or no-drive usually means a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Throttle module fault causes stalling and limp mode (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, stalling, surging, a rough idle, or the car stuck at low speed with an ETS or check engine light.
issues.why: The electronic throttle module gets fouled by carbon and its sensor wears, so the engine computer drops into limp-home mode. Volvo recalled cars for a software fix (06V-441) and changed the part during 2002.
issues.next: If power drops, move to a safe spot. Run your VIN for the recall and ask a Volvo dealer about any remaining throttle module coverage; otherwise the module is replaced.

issues.t: ABS module fails and turns on warning lights
issues.sym: ABS and TRACS (traction control) lights come on, sometimes going away after a cold restart.
issues.why: Solder joints on the ABS control module circuit board crack with age, especially in cold weather. Normal braking remains, but ABS and traction control are lost.
issues.next: Brakes still work without ABS, so drive gently and leave more room in wet or icy weather. Have the wheel speed sensors checked first, then repair or replace the module.

issues.t: Clogged PCV system pushes out oil seals
issues.sym: Oil around the engine and under the plastic cover, smoke or pressure at the dipstick tube, oil smells through the vents, and eventually leaking seals.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system on the 5-cylinder turbo engine clogs with sludge, so pressure builds inside the engine and forces oil past the seals.
issues.next: Have the PCV system checked and cleaned or replaced before it blows the rear main seal, which is a much bigger job. Keep up with oil changes.

issues.t: Soft top stuck or constant roof warning chime
issues.sym: The convertible top will not open or close, the top switch light blinks, or a warning chime sounds over and over while driving.
issues.why: The power top relies on a chain of small position switches (microswitches), a relay and a control module. A failed switch, a bent seat stop or a module fault makes the system think the top is not latched.
issues.next: Make sure the top and its cover are fully latched before driving. A shop that knows Volvo convertibles can test the switches; a single bad switch is a much simpler fix than a module.

issues.t: Water leaks into the trunk or cabin past the soft top
issues.sym: Damp carpets, water in the trunk after rain, or the rear window seal lifting.
issues.why: Drain tubes for the convertible top clog or get crimped, and the seal around the rear glass can fail in strong sun.
issues.next: Clear the top drains and check the boot-area seals. A failing rear window seal may need professional repair or a new top.

issues.t: Immobilizer stops the car from starting
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, or starts and shuts off right away. It often works after several tries and gets worse over time.
issues.why: The immobilizer antenna ring around the ignition switch, or the immobilizer module, stops reading the key chip reliably.
issues.next: Try your spare key and keep the key away from other keys and cards. A shop can confirm with codes; replacing the antenna ring or module is the usual fix.

issues.t: Turn signals may not flash (recall)
issues.sym: Turn signals that work intermittently or not at all.
issues.why: Recall 00V-405: a fault can stop the turn signals from warning other drivers.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall; the fix is free.

issues.t: Door pops ajar while driving
issues.sym: A door-open warning at highway speed, the door visibly loose or rattling, or the window dropping slightly. Many owners notice it with the top down.
issues.why: Many owner reports describe the latch not holding the door fully shut. No recall covers the C70, and dealers often cannot reproduce it.
issues.next: If the warning comes on, slow down and pull over to shut the door firmly. Have the latch and striker inspected and replaced if worn; do not carry passengers until fixed.

issues.t: Retractable hardtop faults and roof error messages
issues.sym: The hardtop stops partway, will not open or close, or shows a roof error and chime.
issues.why: Water can reach the roof module and wiring, connectors corrode, harnesses chafe, and the hydraulic pump valves can stick. Volvo ran service campaigns on 2006-2007 cars to add a water shield, grease connectors and reroute wiring.
issues.next: Do not force the roof. Ask a Volvo dealer whether your car had the roof service campaigns, and have the roof system scanned for codes.

issues.t: Hardtop rattles, wind noise and water leaks
issues.sym: Rattles and thumps from the roof and trunk, whistling wind, or water at the windows and trunk after rain.
issues.why: The folding hardtop has many seals and joints that can shift out of adjustment, and the windshield-top seal can come loose.
issues.next: Have the seals and roof alignment checked. Leaks are worth fixing early because water can damage the roof electronics.

issues.t: Clogged PCV oil trap causes leaks and codes
issues.sym: Check engine light, a whistle or hiss, oil leaks around the engine, or crankcase pressure faults.
issues.why: The PCV oil trap on the 2.5L turbo clogs with sludge, creating wrong crankcase pressure that pushes oil out of seals.
issues.next: Have the oil trap replaced with an oil change. Ignoring it can lead to bigger seal leaks.

issues.t: Battery drains overnight
issues.sym: A dead or weak battery after the car sits, sometimes with window or alarm glitches.
issues.why: Early cars could draw about 2 amps with the car off because of infotainment software; Volvo released a software update in a service campaign.
issues.next: Ask a Volvo dealer whether the software updates were applied. Have the battery and charging system tested.

issues.t: Alarm siren sounds for no reason
issues.sym: The alarm goes off by itself or will not shut off.
issues.why: A central control module software fault; Volvo fixed it with a software update in a service campaign.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the campaign software update.

issues.t: Trunk lid opens on its own or shows open
issues.sym: A "Trunk Lid Open" message or the trunk popping open unexpectedly.
issues.why: Water can get into the trunk lid switch connector and later corrode it. A service campaign greased the connector.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the campaign was done; a corroded connector is a small repair.

issues.t: Rear tires wear fast and unevenly
issues.sym: Rear tires wearing on the inner edges, feathered or scalloped tread, sometimes in well under 20,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners report rear alignment drifting out and worn rear camber arms on these cars.
issues.next: Have a four-wheel alignment done and the rear arms and bushings inspected when you replace tires.

issues.t: A/C compressor or clutch fails
issues.sym: Air conditioning blows warm, or cooling comes and goes.
issues.why: The compressor clutch can slip or the compressor can fail.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures and clutch checked before replacing parts.

issues.t: Power steering hose can burst (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden heavy steering, power steering fluid leaking, or a whining pump.
issues.why: Recall 08V-329: a power steering return hose was not cured properly and can rupture.
issues.next: If steering suddenly gets heavy, slow down and pull over. Check your VIN; the hose is replaced free.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can leak internally (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal needs more force or goes lower over time.
issues.why: Recall 08V-101: a soft coating in the master cylinder wears the seal so fluid leaks inside it, reducing braking.
issues.next: Get the free recall repair right away if not done; have the brakes checked if the pedal feels different.

issues.t: Left door handle cable may be attached wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No obvious symptom.
issues.why: Recall 07V-218: the left door handle cable may have been misassembled, so the door may not meet crash rules.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers reposition the cable free.

issues.t: Tire pressure label misprinted (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; the label may list the wrong tire pressure.
issues.why: Recall 11V-508: on cars with the optional spare tire kit, the tire information label was misprinted.
issues.next: Use the pressure in your owner's manual and get the free corrected label.
